blocking_review_findings.claim: fc_cross_user and fc_owner_unfiltered do not assert that update_col is actually updatable by authenticated. If a later column lock revokes UPDATE on the chosen column, the UPDATE probes return 'none' via 'permission denied' and pass without testing RLS (full-chain.probes.sql:128 and :355, '-- update_col is a column A may update where one exists' at :301-302 is a comment, not a check).
blocking_review_findings.so_what: The owner tripwire and unfiltered-UPDATE probes can go silently vacuous on a table whose UPDATE stays on the FC-CLIENT-WRITES allow-list.
blocking_review_findings.fix: When has_any_column_privilege('authenticated', rel, 'UPDATE') holds, vassert has_column_privilege('authenticated', rel, coalesce(update_col, owner_col), 'UPDATE') in fc_cross_user.

previous_blocking_review_findings_round0.issue: FC-CROSS-USER and FC-STORAGE do not prove cross-user denial for writes, although both PASS lines claim it (full-chain.probes.sql:412, cases/240-full-chain-replay.sh:300). Filtered writes by user A are masked by the SELECT policy. The unfiltered UPDATE/DELETE probes run only as stranger C, who owns no row (full-chain.probes.sql:154 and :286-293). So any UPDATE/DELETE policy keyed on 'the caller owns some row' never fires. No probe tries re-owning a row with UPDATE SET owner_col = <other user>. This is the F095 core assertion (decision 3: cross-user denial for every user-owned table), claimed fixed.

previous_blocking_review_findings_round0.fix:
In fc_cross_user and FC-STORAGE, add unfiltered write probes run as user A, who owns rows. Inside the rolled-back transaction, as postgres, create a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE FOR EACH ROW tripwire trigger on the probed relation, named to sort first:
- It RAISEs a dedicated SQLSTATE such as P0102 when to_jsonb(OLD)->>owner_col (for storage: (storage.foldername(OLD.name))[1]) is in `theirs`.
- Otherwise it RETURNs NULL, so A's own rows are skipped and no constraint fires.
As A, run UPDATE rel SET <update_col> = DEFAULT and DELETE FROM rel with no filter and require that P0102 never fires, then drop the trigger.
Add a re-own probe: as A, fc_reach_and_undo(format('UPDATE public.%I SET %I = %L', rel, owner_col, theirs[1])) must be 'none' (42501 counts as none).
Mutation-prove with mu1, mu13 and mu3. Keep the PASS lines matching what is asserted.

previous_blocking_review_findings_round0.issue: Under the probes' own unfiltered-write threat model (header lines 11-14 and 242-246), FC-CROSS-USER and FC-STORAGE cannot detect UPDATE policies whose USING is broader than their WITH CHECK, or the reverse. fc_reach_and_undo (line 115) and fc_reached (line 97) map EVERY 42501 to 'none'/0. That includes 'new row violates row-level security policy', which is raised BY a row the USING clause reached. The unfiltered probe (line 288, and line 155 for storage) sets a non-owner column to DEFAULT, so WITH CHECK always fails on another user's row and hides the reach. No probe tries to move a user's own rows into another account (an UPDATE of owner_col). So a cross-user write path ships green, although the probe header says rows cannot be 'changed ... by filtered or unfiltered writes' and the commit says scratch runs kill 'any-row ... update policies'.
previous_blocking_review_findings_round0.evidence: Mutations run in my own container on a copy of the reviewed tree, through the unmodified case 240 (run240.sh). (mutA) Added a migration that replaces period_logs' UPDATE policy with USING (true) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id). Result: case 240 exits 0, with 'PASS FC-CROSS-USER period_logs' and the full PASS line (mutA/run.log). Exploit on that database (exploit-reparent.sql): A runs the unfiltered `UPDATE period_logs SET user_id = A`, which is what a PATCH without a filter sends. Before: B owns 1 row. After: B owns 0 and A reads it. On the real chain the same exploit leaves B owning 1. (mutB) symptom_logs USING (auth.uid() = user_id) WITH CHECK (true), plus a storage.objects UPDATE policy USING (bucket_id = 'lab-files') WITH CHECK (own folder). Result: case 240 exits 0, with 'PASS FC-STORAGE' and 'PASS FC-CROSS-USER symptom_logs' (mutB/run.log). Exploit (exploit-mutB.sql): A's unfiltered UPDATE moves her symptom log into B's account ('B owns symptom logs: 1'), and `UPDATE storage.objects SET name = auth.uid()::text || '/' || gen_random_uuid()::text || '.pdf'` moves B's lab file into A's folder ('A now reads lab files: 1', 'objects left in B's folder: 0'). Filtered writes are safe even under these mutations, because the SELECT policy also applies to the new row: I observed 'new row violates row-level security policy' for a WHERE-filtered plant. So the hole affects exactly the unfiltered vector the probes claim to cover, the same class as the C15/C17 survivors the implementer fixed. Whether production's PostgREST blocks WHERE-less writes (pg-safeupdate) cannot be checked from the repo. There is no live defect: every UPDATE policy in the replayed chain has identical USING and WITH CHECK (pg_policies query q1.sql), and storage.objects has no UPDATE policy.
